partner_context.their_ambition: Transport for NSW runs one of the world's iconic ferry networks across Sydney Harbour and the Parramatta River, and has committed to a zero-emission bus and ferry future for Greater Sydney.
partner_context.their_pressure: The harbour is congested, the road network saturated, and the ageing diesel ferry fleet is under a decarbonization mandate. Commuter demand keeps growing along the river and across the harbour, but conventional ferries are slow and the fleet must be replaced.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier delivers zero-emission vessels that are also faster and smoother — taking the high-frequency harbour and river commuter legs while satisfying the clean-fleet mandate, and unlocking new premium links the network has never had.

hero.title: Navier × Transport for NSW — the harbour, flying and clean
hero.subtitle: Foiling-electric vessels for Sydney's zero-emission ferry future.
hero.what_we_do_together: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet that satisfies NSW's zero-emission ferry mandate while flying faster and quieter than the diesel ferries it replaces. The partnership pairs Navier's platform, captain training and certification path with Transport for NSW's wharves, integrated-ticketing system and commuter demand — modernizing one of the world's great ferry networks.

why_now: NSW has committed to a zero-emission ferry future and is replacing its ageing diesel fleet. Sydney Harbour and the Parramatta River carry dense, growing commuter demand on a saturated road network. A tier that is clean AND faster AND smoother is exactly what the mandate and the commuter need.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the existing Sydney Ferries network — Circular Quay, Parramatta, Manly, Watsons Bay, the Olympic Park river run — taking high-frequency commuter legs integrated with Opal ticketing, while conventional ferries keep the heaviest trunk routes. Commuters step from train or metro to foil to wharf.

journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A faster, silent, zero-emission foiling commute — smoother across the heads' swell.

journeys_unlocked.today: A diesel ferry or congested eastern-suburbs roads.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A quick clean harbour hop to the eastern beaches.

journeys_unlocked.today: A river ferry or a congested road/rail combination.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A fast foiling river link for events and the growing western precinct.

journeys_unlocked.today: A long road or rail trip up the coast.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A premium coastal foiling line-haul north of the harbour.

differentiation.why_navier: The only foiling-electric platform that meets NSW's zero-emission ferry mandate while being faster and quieter than the diesel fleet — software-defined, autonomy-ready, and integrable with Opal ticketing and existing wharves.

proof_points.evidence: NSW has committed to a zero-emission bus and ferry future for Greater Sydney.

proof_points.claim: Ferry demand is large and iconic.
proof_points.evidence: Sydney Ferries carry tens of millions of trips a year across the harbour and Parramatta River.
Opal contactless ticketing spans ferries, trains, metro and buses — a ready multimodal backbone.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Can it handle the harbour heads' swell?
objections.response: The foil flies above the chop, giving a smoother ride than a diesel ferry across the Manly heads. Pioneer II covers all the harbour and river commuter legs all-electric; Quanta-LR carries the longer coastal runs to Newcastle/Central Coast.

objections.concern: Does it integrate with Opal and the wharves?
objections.response: Yes — it runs from existing Sydney Ferries wharves and integrates with Opal contactless ticketing; no new terminal infrastructure required, only a berth pedestal for charging.

objections.concern: Is it a procurement fit for a public authority?
objections.response: Phased and contractible like any ferry-fleet renewal — start on a high-demand commuter corridor, prove the unit economics and reliability, then scale across the network as diesel vessels retire.

objections.concern: What about charging across the network?
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at key wharves; the harbour's short legs sit well inside the all-electric range with charging at terminus wharves between runs.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Manly & inner-harbour commuter
phases.narrative: Launch on the marquee Circular Quay ↔ Manly run and the inner-harbour hops (Watsons Bay, Rose Bay, Taronga) — the highest-frequency, most visible commuter legs.
phases.rationale: Prove the mandate-compliant faster-and-smoother tier on Sydney's most iconic ferry corridor.

phases.label: Phase 2 — Parramatta River network
phases.narrative: Scale up the Parramatta River — Circular Quay to Parramatta, Olympic Park and the western precincts — the fast-growing western-city commuter spine.
phases.rationale: Serve the western city's growth corridor where road congestion is worst.

phases.label: Phase 3 — Greater Sydney + coastal corridor
phases.narrative: Roughly 20 vessels forming a zero-emission foiling layer across Greater Sydney's harbour and river network, with Quanta-LR opening the premium coastal corridor to Newcastle and the Central Coast.
phases.rationale: Complete the network renewal and add the new coastal links the network never had.

featured_routes.label: Circular Quay ↔ Watsons Bay / Rose Bay

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, certification path and the operating playbook for harbour and river commuter service.
the_ask.partner_brings: Wharf access, Opal ticketing integration, the route-by-route rollout sequence and the public-transport procurement pathway.
the_ask.next_step: Launch a Manly or Parramatta pilot corridor in 2027 and scale across the network as the diesel fleet retires.

close.title: The harbour, finally flying.
close.body: Sydney already committed to zero-emission ferries. Navier is the tier that makes clean also mean faster and smoother — modernizing one of the world's great ferry networks while meeting the mandate.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging' excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

steady_state.tam_framing: Tens of millions of ferry trips a year on a network under a zero-emission mandate.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a zero-emission foiling ferry layer across Greater Sydney — faster, smoother and cleaner across the harbour, the river and the coast.
